content.value_statement: Skool owners need pricing that funds growth without adding too many offers at once. This skill applies CAC math, Hormozi mechanisms, and Skool setup guidance.
actual_capabilities: Diagnoses the community stage using CAC, 30-day revenue, and acquisition reliability.
Calculates 30-day cash gaps with deterministic Python helper functions.
Maps Skool models across free, subscription, freemium, tiers, and one-time payments.
Recommends one or two Hormozi mechanisms with prerequisites and source citations.
Builds implementation roadmaps with pricing, setup steps, tests, and success metrics.
limitations: Requires accurate CAC, revenue, member, churn, and conversion inputs for useful analysis.
Does not write finished sales copy, course content, emails, or customer avatar profiles.
Uses benchmark ranges, not guaranteed conversion or churn predictions.
Focuses on Skool monetization, not full business strategy outside the platform.

use_cases.title: Launch a monetized community
use_cases.description: Choose an initial model, identify needed inputs, and plan the first revenue mechanism.

use_cases.title: Repair weak 30-day cash
use_cases.description: Compare CAC against first-month revenue and select a realistic upsell, annual, or one-time purchase path.

use_cases.title: Simplify a crowded offer stack
use_cases.description: Audit tiers, upsells, and downsells, then sequence changes so one mechanism is tested at a time.

prompt_templates.title: Start a diagnosis
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to diagnose my Skool money model. My CAC is [amount], monthly price is [amount], paid members are [count], and my goal is [goal].

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate a pricing change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to evaluate a Skool pricing change from [current model] to [new model]. Compare 30-day cash, member experience, and implementation risks.

prompt_templates.title: Design a tier strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design two or three Skool tiers for [audience]. Include pricing logic, upgrade triggers, one-time purchases, and a 60-day test plan.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a mechanism
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to validate whether [mechanism idea] truly matches a Hormozi mechanism. Cite prerequisites, flag mismatches, and recommend the safest next experiment.

output_examples.input: CAC is $300 and the only offer is a $97 monthly Skool subscription.
output: Stage 2 diagnosis because first-month revenue is below CAC.
Gap analysis showing the minimum added cash needed to cover acquisition.
Recommendation to test one annual or one-time purchase mechanism before adding more complexity.

output_examples.input: A free Skool group wants paid upgrades and classroom products.
output: Freemium model review with upgrade tiers, buy-now classroom offers, and affiliate implications.
Skool setup checklist for member access, course visibility, and pricing tests.
Revenue projection ranges that separate conservative, realistic, and optimistic assumptions.

output_examples.input: An owner wants three tiers, a giveaway, annual discount, course upsell, and downsell.
output: Complexity warning that explains why too many mechanisms weaken measurement.
One prioritized mechanism based on stage, goal, CAC, and implementation effort.
Staged 30-60 day rollout plan with success metrics before adding the next offer.

best_practices: Bring CAC, member counts, prices, churn, and conversion rates before asking for a full roadmap.
Ask for one priority outcome, such as more 30-day cash or better tier upgrades.
Review the cited mechanism definition before implementing any recommendation.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for guaranteed revenue or exact conversion predictions.
Do not implement several mechanisms at once without isolating test results.
Do not use the skill for sales copy, general content creation, or non-Skool strategy.

faq.question: Does this skill calculate revenue projections?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses the included Python helpers to calculate stage, gap, cash, MRR, and tier relationships.

faq.question: Does it need my CAC?
faq.answer: Yes. CAC is required for stage diagnosis and 30-day cash targets. It can help estimate CAC from spend data.

faq.question: Can it design Skool tiers?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare freemium, subscription, tiered, and one-time payment structures for Skool communities.

faq.question: Will it guarantee better revenue?
faq.answer: No. It provides frameworks, ranges, tests, and warnings. Results depend on traffic quality, offer fit, execution, and retention.

faq.question: Does it write sales pages or emails?
faq.answer: No. It can shape positioning and offer structure, but it does not produce full sales copy or content.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Python is useful for its calculation helper.
